summary: This is a clean restack of three components. Each was checked alone on the same base (b99b1dd) and wins on its own disjoint (layer, m) cells, so per-row attribution plus kernel names makes one combined run readable without companions, and it is the best use of the last bf16 check. The headline will probably sit at or just past the top of best's CI (about 1.238-1.243 against 1.2398), so promotion depends on the six target rows. The risks are prepare-time budget and the unpooler gate flipping off silently, not a design flaw.
justification: A: The mechanism is plausible and the profile supports it. Router m=1/8 runs at 5.4-5.5 us against a 1.8 us floor, and about 0.7-0.8 us of that is a vectorized_elementwise memset node, which the cluster kernel removes (solo: 5.38->4.98, 5.47->4.93). Unpooler slice m=1/8 runs at 6.0-6.2 us against a 1.7-1.8 us floor; ouns_kernel gave 5.34/5.41 solo, and in the prepare gate it won about 1.10x net of an empty graph on both m. At m=128, pooler 25.0 us and unpooler 20.0 us sit well above their 14.6 us floor, and NN-layout nvjet gave 22.6/19.0 solo. The expected directions are consistent: six faster rows on cells no other component touches, flat elsewhere. The summed row savings are about 0.4+0.5+0.8+0.6+2.4+1.0 us, and in each solo run they moved the headline +0.0 to +0.7%, so +1.3-1.8% combined is a fair estimate. That is roughly the CI half-width, so the headline alone may stay 'unproven-vs-best'. Weakest link: the unpooler cell. Master's own unpooler decode_1 reading spans 5.34-6.15 us across four runs, so its 'faster' is partly noise. The solo NN-layout run also logged an unpooler decode_1 gain with NO change on that row, which shows the noise is as large as the claimed effect. Also, ouns_cl is decided per prepare() by a timed gate (both m=1 and m=8 must reach >=1.02 net), so the cluster path can silently turn off in one or both rotated states. Judge that row only on the printed '[ouns] PATH CHOSEN' line for each state plus ouns_kernel in the profile. A second weak point: the earlier NN-layout narrowing on the older master (pooler-unpooler-m128-nn-layout-gated, a8bb42a) was a 1.1953 regression with many off-target losses. The b99b1dd restack run (1.2282) suggests those losses were drift, but the NN gain is still only two solo readings.
confounders: bf16-restack-m16-swapab-router-swapab-m32 (base b99b1dd): it put router m<=32 on _router_swapab_kernel + memset. The router-cluster win at m=1/8 is measured against that kernel, and most of it is the deleted memset node. If the swap-AB router were retuned or reverted, the cluster margin would change. This is not a confound for this run: the base is fixed and the same base was used in all three solo runs.

bf16-restack-m16-swapab-router-swapab-m32 / bf16-m16-swapab-wgmma-extend: ouns_kernel competes with the swapab16 unpooler-slice path (4.3-4.4 us kernel). The in-prepare gate compares against exactly that incumbent, so the comparison is internally controlled. No confound beyond the gate's noise.

router-triton-hilo-fused-control-splitk-all-m / router-hilo-at-m8: these set the hi+lo BF16 router numerics that router_kernel<8,8> must reproduce with fp32 accumulation, a correctness coupling rather than a timing one. The self-check at m {1,5,8} covers it.

sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity: it fixes cuBLAS dispatch above m=32. The NN branch is inserted before that fallback for pooler/unpooler at 65..128 only, so a pooler/unpooler verify_16 change is the NN layout itself. Confirm with an *_NNT nvjet name in the profile.

Shared drift (not a landed hypothesis): o verify_16/decode_32 got +4-8% slower in all three solo runs with unchanged kernels, and router verify_16 lost in two of three with hilo unchanged. Expect it again and do not attribute it to the restack.
interference: No companions. The three components touch disjoint (layer, m) cells and each has already been measured alone on the identical base (d323ce8ef6a54fde, e557d92969864449, 92cd4e758a924ca0). Each would-be control already exists, so a gain or loss on a target row reads directly against both master and that component's solo number. The only real interaction channels are prepare-side: two load_inline builds plus two prepared states against the 300 s prepare budget, ext-name collisions, and the GPU state left by one component's gate or self-check while the other times. None of these is something an A/B run would resolve better than the run's own log lines. An ab-revert of a landed hypothesis is not meaningful because every component targets cells that landed work owns, and companions cannot run today anyway. The one ambiguity a companion would resolve, whether a combined headline below the summed estimate comes from interaction or noise, is better answered by per-row paired ratios against the three solo runs.
rules_flags: Prepare-time timed gate (unpooler ouns_cl, a 41-rep cold-flush graph replay on synthetic data) is the same pattern as the open cuBLASLt algo-pick rules question. TASK.md does not forbid untimed autotuning in prepare, and nothing is derived from data, but if the user rules against it, replace the gate with a constant route (1 <= m <= 8, n == 1024) as the hypothesis already notes. Do not drop the self-check.

load_inline invokes nvcc/ninja as child processes, and TASK.md says submissions that 'start processes' are rejected. Both component patches passed the checker in their solo runs, so this is accepted in practice. Keep the build exactly as in the patches: in-process load_inline, no explicit subprocess.

The component patches use try/except around load_inline, the self-check and the gate inside prepare(). That is fine. Make sure no try/except, print, or host sync leaks into kernel_fn during the hand merge.

The NN layout stores W.t().contiguous() bf16 copies of pooler and unpooler (+134 MB per state, x2 states). This is a lossless same-precision repack, so it is allowed. Confirm it fits device memory next to the 256 MB gate flush buffer, which must be freed before prepare returns.

Routing must read only shapes and prepare-fixed flags (ouns_cl, router_cluster_ok). Because the two rotated states can disagree on ouns_cl, the dispatch must read the flag from the state passed in, never from a module global.
open_questions: Does prepare() fit 300 s with two cold load_inline builds (if the torch extension cache is not warm on the judge), two states, the unpooler gate and the new A/B/A/B graph self-check? Print per-phase timings. If the router build fails or times out it falls back silently, and the run becomes a two-component restack.
Did both prepared states choose the same paths? Require the '[ouns] PATH CHOSEN' and router-cluster self-check lines twice in the log before reading the target rows.

If the headline lands inside best's CI but all six target rows show the expected kernel names and paired ratios above 1, is per-row promotion enough under the current promotion rule, or does landing need the user's approval (PENDING_USER 04:36Z already says it does)?

If the combined run shows the router or unpooler m<=8 gains smaller than solo, is that because the second cluster extension changes co-resident cluster occupancy, or is it noise? The ouns cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters line (45 vs 16 needed) should be re-printed to rule out the first.
